---
title: "Markups and the wage share"
page-layout: full
toc: false
---

Firms set their price as a markup, $\mu$, on unit labour cost. With labour
productivity $\lambda$ (output per worker) and nominal wage $w$, unit labour
cost is $w / \lambda$, so

$$
p = (1 + \mu) \frac{w}{\lambda}
\qquad \text{and so} \qquad
\frac{w}{p} = \frac{\lambda}{1 + \mu} .
$$

This is the *markup line*: the real wage implied by firms' pricing. Output is
$\overline{Y} = \lambda L$, where $L$ is employment, and it is divided between
real wage income, $\overline{WB} = (w/p) L$, and real profit income,
$\overline{\Pi} = (\lambda - w/p) L$. The wage share of output is

$$
\frac{\overline{WB}}{\overline{Y}} = \frac{w/p}{\lambda} = \frac{1}{1 + \mu} ,
$$

so it depends only on the markup. Changing productivity or employment changes
the size of the two rectangles, but not how output is split between them.
The idea is Michał Kalecki's "degree of monopoly" (1930s).

Press **Pin these lines** to keep the current diagram as dashed lines, then change
the sliders to compare. For example, pin with a markup of 25%, then raise it to
60%: the real wage falls, and the wage share falls from 80% to 62.5%, with
productivity and employment unchanged.

::: {.sim-layout}

::: {.sim-controls}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof lambda = Inputs.range([0.5, 2], {value: 1, step: 0.05, label: "Productivity, λ"})
viewof mu = Inputs.range([0, 1], {value: 0.25, step: 0.01, label: "Markup, μ"})
viewof L = Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 60, step: 1, label: "Employment, L"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Outcomes for productivity lam, markup m and employment l.
function outcomes(lam, m, l) {
  const realWage = lam / (1 + m)
  return {lambda: lam, mu: m, L: l, realWage, output: lam * l, wages: realWage * l,
    profits: (lam - realWage) * l, wageShare: 1 / (1 + m)}
}
now = outcomes(lambda, mu, L)

// The pinned diagram, if any, kept until it is cleared.
mutable pinned = null
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<p>${Object.assign(html`<button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary">Pin these lines</button>`, {onclick: () => { mutable pinned = now }})}
${Object.assign(html`<button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary">Clear</button>`, {onclick: () => { mutable pinned = null }})}</p>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
pct = x => `${(100 * x).toFixed(1)}%`
// One row of the readout: the current value, and the pinned value if there is one.
row = (label, key, format = x => x.toFixed(2)) => html`<tr><td>${label}</td>
  <td style="text-align:right">${format(now[key])}</td>
  ${pinned ? html`<td style="text-align:right; opacity:0.6">${format(pinned[key])}</td>` : ""}</tr>`

html`<table class="table table-sm" style="font-size: 0.9em">
  <thead><tr><th></th><th style="text-align:right">now</th>${pinned ? html`<th style="text-align:right; opacity:0.6">pinned</th>` : ""}</tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    ${row("Real wage, w/p", "realWage")}
    ${row("Output, λL", "output", x => x.toFixed(1))}
    ${row("Real wage income", "wages", x => x.toFixed(1))}
    ${row("Real profit income", "profits", x => x.toFixed(1))}
    ${row("Wage share", "wageShare", pct)}
    ${row("Profit share", "wageShare", x => pct(1 - x))}
  </tbody>
</table>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const blue = "#2a78d6"
  const yMax = 2.2, xMax = 100
  // Labels just left of the vertical axis, in place of tick marks.
  const axisLabels = [{y: now.lambda, text: "λ"}, {y: now.realWage, text: "w/p"}]
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 620,
    height: 460,
    marginLeft: 50,
    x: {label: "Employment, L", domain: [0, xMax], ticks: []},
    y: {label: null, domain: [0, yMax], ticks: []},
    marks: [
      // Real wage income and real profit income.
      Plot.rect([now], {x1: 0, x2: "L", y1: 0, y2: "realWage", fill: blue, fillOpacity: 0.18}),
      Plot.rect([now], {x1: 0, x2: "L", y1: "realWage", y2: "lambda", fill: blue, fillOpacity: 0.4}),
      // The pinned diagram, dashed.
      pinned ? Plot.ruleY([pinned.lambda, pinned.realWage], {stroke: "currentColor", strokeOpacity: 0.5, strokeDasharray: "5,4"}) : null,
      pinned ? Plot.ruleX([pinned.L], {y1: 0, y2: pinned.lambda, stroke: "currentColor", strokeOpacity: 0.5, strokeDasharray: "5,4"}) : null,
      pinned ? Plot.text([{y: pinned.lambda, text: "pinned λ"}, {y: pinned.realWage, text: "pinned w/p"}], {
        x: xMax, y: "y", text: "text", textAnchor: "end", dy: 10, fillOpacity: 0.5
      }) : null,
      // Productivity and the markup line.
      Plot.ruleY([now.lambda, now.realWage], {stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.text([{y: now.lambda, text: "productivity"}, {y: now.realWage, text: "markup line"}], {
        x: xMax, y: "y", text: "text", textAnchor: "end", dy: -9, fillOpacity: 0.7
      }),
      Plot.text(axisLabels, {x: 0, y: "y", text: "text", textAnchor: "end", dx: -8, fontSize: 14}),
      Plot.text([now], {x: "L", y: 0, text: () => "L", dy: 14, fontSize: 14}),
      // Name each rectangle when it is big enough to hold the label.
      now.L > 30 && now.lambda - now.realWage > 0.15
        ? Plot.text([now], {x: d => d.L / 2, y: d => (d.lambda + d.realWage) / 2, text: () => "real profit income, (λ − w/p)L"})
        : null,
      now.L > 30 && now.realWage > 0.15
        ? Plot.text([now], {x: d => d.L / 2, y: d => d.realWage / 2, text: () => "real wage income, (w/p)L"})
        : null,
      Plot.ruleX([0]),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  })
}
```
